# spw.quest

> Spw is a notation for a reading you can compare: a mark says what a word is doing, and a brace says which slot it fills. An answer written in Spw can be parsed, compared, and opened as a card or a canvas.

An address and a line together, as in "spw.quest rpgwednesday<card>", ask for an answer written in Spw. The line names the subject and its <concept> names the kind of answer. An answer is plain Spw text, with no code fence and no sentence before it. A person setting up a repository wants [the recipe](https://spw.quest/init) instead.

A line is word[mode]{body}(scene)<concept>, and only the word is required.

- word: what the line is about, one name with no spaces.
- [mode]: how it is being seen.
- {body}: what belongs to it. A dot makes one name, a comma holds a company, a semicolon keeps an order, ~> is a path.
- (scene): where or when it stands.
- <concept>: what kind of thing it is.

A mark goes right before a word, with no space after it:

- ~ potential: Keep a path open without taking it.
- ? wonder: Open a question you can close again.
- ! action: Commit a move so its consequence can be seen.
- * value: Mark what carries weight here.
- . ground: Come back to the local default.
- ^ ascension: Lift parts into one relation you can inspect.
- # vibration: Name a structure so it can be found again.
- @ perspective: Say who is looking, and from where.
- & subject: Name what the relation is about.
- = configuration: Keep this here, under this name.
- % measure: Compare, weigh, or level the field.
- $ substrate: Name what carries the charge: time, money, memory, attention.

Quoted text takes double quotes. #>name names a file or a line, and #:kind says what kind of file it is.

A word<card> is the line with its [mode], {body} and (scene) filled in from what is known, then a seed card, and a seed card always names its template. For a thing you know about, ^seed[Session] has the fields date, scene, turn, carry and revisit, and a field with nothing known is left out. Asked garden<card>, this is an answer, and pasted on spwashi.com it opens as a card:

    garden[weekly]{beds, compost, seedlings}(saturday)<card>
    ^seed[Session]{
      scene: "a shared plot, tended on Saturdays"
      carry: "the beds planted last week"
      revisit: "what survived the frost?"
    }

For a word you know nothing about, not knowing is the card. ^seed[Wonder.Prompt] has the fields question, tension, material, relay and revisit, and each says what would have to be found out:

    nightmarket<card>
    ^seed[Wonder.Prompt]{
      question: "what is nightmarket, and who keeps it?"
      tension: "the name is all that was given"
      relay: "whoever named it"
      revisit: "once a page says what it is"
    }

A word<question> is the question, what is expected, and the probe that would answer it:

    ?["Will the seedlings survive a frost?"]{
      ~#expect: "the covered bed holds and the open bed does not"
      !probe{ "read both beds the morning after the first frost" }
    }

A word<change> says what happened, what changed, and how it was checked:

    #[episode]{
      ~[scene]{ the open bed lost its seedlings to a frost }
      ![change]{ every bed is covered before dusk in November }
      *[verify]{ all four beds came through the next frost }
    }

Any other <concept> is the line with its slots filled and one plain sentence:

    garden[weekly]{beds, compost}(saturday)<plot>
    *says = "a shared plot, tended on Saturdays"

Facts about a word come from the Card address below, which lists what the site holds for it. On X an answer fits 280 characters and has no @ directly before a name, since that notifies the account; a # before a letter shows as a tag. A link to https://spw.quest/card?line= with the line percent-encoded unfurls as a link card.

## Addresses

Every address below answers with a page that reads with no script, except Canvas.

- [Card](https://spw.quest/card.txt?line=rpgwednesday%3Ccard%3E): You hold a line and want what the site holds for its word before answering it, as text. line: one line, 200 characters. /card with the same line is a small page that unfurls as a link card, and spw.quest/ followed by the line itself answers the same. Example: line = rpgwednesday<card>.
- [Pivot](https://spw.quest/pivot?line=home%5Bhook%5D%7Bsoftware.art%7D): You hold one line and want the lines one change away from it, grouped by the slot each turns. A turn that lands on a line a page already holds says which page, with a link to it. line: one line, 200 characters; past that it is cut and the page says so. In a browser, #turn-mode, #turn-body, #turn-subject, #turn-scope or #turn-projection scrolls to one slot; a fetch gets the whole page. Example: line = home[hook]{software.art}.
- [Find](https://spw.quest/specimens?q=recipe%5B*%5D): You want every line on spwashi.com with some shape: the same word through other lenses, the same lens on other words. q: slots to match, with * for any value. The page is about 280 KB whatever is asked: the answer comes first, and the whole shelf follows it. Example: q = recipe[*].
- [Compare](https://spw.quest/specimens?a=h-capsule&b=h-induct_join): You hold two shelf lines and want the slots they share and the slot where they part. a, b: shelf ids, as Find prints them. The page is about 280 KB whatever is asked: the answer comes first, and the whole shelf follows it. Example: a = h-capsule, b = h-induct_join.
- [Take apart](https://spw.quest/build?script=~door%5Bajar%5D%7Bhinge%7D): You hold a file, or a line among others, and want what a tool reads from it and each slot's alternatives from the file's own lines. script: up to 1800 characters in an address. line: which of its lines to take apart, counted from 1. Example: script = ~door[ajar]{hinge}.
- [Read a file](https://spw.quest/?example=record): You want a whole example of a kind of file (a log, a catalog record, a question with its probe) and what a tool reads from it. example: notebook, record, vocabulary, question, script, revision, persona, calibration, perspectives, loops, gradient, syntax, headings, perform, outline, recurrence, laws, pantry, pipeline, review, records, surfaces, primitives, algorithms, role or onboarding. at: a name in the file, to land on its line. Example: example = record.
- [Check a line](https://spw.quest/read?step=act&line=~door): You are learning one mark and want a single line checked against that panel's rule. step: write, act, hold, name, point, ask or grow. line: up to 400 characters. Example: step = act, line = ~door.
- [At rest](https://spw.quest/physics?line=home%5Bhook%5D%7Bsoftware.art%7D): You want a line drawn as bodies at rest, with the laws that placed them. line: one line. Example: line = home[hook]{software.art}.
- [Canvas](https://spw.quest/canvas?line=home%5Bhook%5D%7Bsoftware.art%7D): You want a person to see a line laid out as a force-directed canvas on factshift.center. It draws with scripts, so a reader without them gets only its chrome: use Pivot to read the line. line: up to 400 characters, or s: a shelf id. Answers with a redirect to factshift.center. Example: line = home[hook]{software.art}.

## Reference

- [Marks and braces](https://spw.quest/#operators): each mark and brace pair, what it reads as, and what the runtime does with it.
- [Constructs](https://spw.quest/constructs): the shapes a line takes, each with a pressed example.
- [Dated parser builds](https://spw.quest/parser/): the parser as a file to load on your own page.

## Optional

- [Initialize a repository](https://spw.quest/init): the recipe for mounting Spw Workbench, for an agent asked to set one up.
- [quest.json](https://spw.quest/quest.json): that recipe's facts as data.
- [Every example file](https://spw.quest/llms-full.txt): this index, then each file whole.

## Example files

lab-notebook.spw: Chronological empirical log: dated entries categorized by epistemological kind, allowing automated synthesis of bench progression across cataloging, experimental trials, metric measurements, and landed invariants.

    #>lab_notebook
    #:log #!components #!themes
    @chip: ~"./chip.spw"
    @matte: ~"./themes.spw#matte"

    ^"stream"{
     >>[2026-11-06 09:10] catalog — the chip, in three dialects on one screen: pill, ring, plain
     >>[2026-11-06 11:40] try — the matte theme on the chip: the ring holds its edge, the pill loses it
     >>[2026-11-06 14:05] measure — --shape-panel read 22 times in 11 files, with three fallbacks
     >>[2026-11-06 17:30] land — one inset for every panel on a phone
    }

chip.spw: Bibliographic catalog record grounded in information science: title, cross-reference variants, categorical subjects, and evidentiary provenance.

    #>component_chip
    #:record #!component
    @broader: ~"./control.spw"
    @related: ~"./sigil.spw"
    @tried: ~"./experiment.spw"

    ^"record"{
      title = `chip`
      also_called = #[`pill`, `ring`, `plain`][reg=set]
      subjects = #[`handle`, `operator`, `touch target`][reg=set]
      provenance = `cataloged 2026-11-06 from three screens`
    }[reg=facet]

themes.spw: Controlled vocabulary and ontological schema: canonical preferred terms, non-preferred synonyms, and scoping notes ensuring conceptual alignment.

    #>theme_vocabulary
    #:vocabulary #!themes

    ^"matte"{
      use_for = #[`flat`, `chalk`][reg=set]
      scope = `a surface that takes no light; text sits on it at full contrast`
      broader = `metamaterial`
    }[reg=facet]

    ^"glass"{
      use_for = #[`frosted`, `liquid`][reg=set]
      scope = `a surface that lets what lies beneath show through, refracted`
      broader = `metamaterial`
    }[reg=facet]

experiment.spw: Metacognitive hypothesis testing: an epistemic inquiry pairing an interrogative wonder with an explicit hypothesis, expected outcome, and empirical verification probe.

    #>wonder_ring_on_glass
    @chip: ~"./chip.spw"
    @glass: ~"./themes.spw#glass"
    ?["Does the ring chip read on the glass theme at a phone's width?"]{
      ~#hypothesis: `a ring keeps its edge where a pill's fill washes out`
      ~#expect: `the ring holds 3:1 against the busiest panel; the pill does not`
      !probe{ "screenshot the chip row on glass at 390px and measure each edge's contrast" }
      $%[ring.reads, pill.reads, neither]
    }

session.spw: Procedural session script: sequential operational transitions modeled as ordered path steps, enabling step-by-step execution tracking and state verification.

    #>catalog_session
    #:script #!session
    @record: ~"./chip.spw#record"

    steps = path{~gather; *describe; ^classify; !shelve}
    gather = shelf[ui]{chip.card}<record>

change.spw: Tripartite change episode: context scene, state transformation, and empirical verification criteria—the syntactic contract of every repository mutation.

    #[episode]{
      ~[scene]{ a panel body drew a second wall on a phone, and its text sat on the line }
      ![change]{ a body slot keeps no wall of its own below 45rem }
      *[verify]{ heading, body and first line share one edge on fourteen frames }
    }

archivist.spw: Situated epistemic persona: communicative voice, observational locus, epistemic axioms, and persistent heuristic habits held in regard.

    #>archivist_persona
    #:persona #!library

    ^"persona"{
      voice = `plain, exact, fond of see-also`
      regards = `the component shelf from the reading room`
      affirms = `a record is a promise that a thing can be found again`
      stayed = `the habit of naming where each thing came from`
    }[reg=facet]

calibration.spw: Metacognitive calibration model: pre-task prediction vs. post-task recall with scalar confidence assessments, quantified by a dimensional gradient %.

    #>calibration
    #:study #!metacognition

    ^"before"{
      predict = `I can say why recalling beats rereading`
      confidence = 0.7
    }[reg=facet]

    ^"after"{
      recalled = `two of the three reasons`
      confidence = 0.5
      next = `reread chapter 2 with a question written first`
    }[reg=facet]

    %confidence{before ~> after}

perspectives.spw: Multi-agent deictic perspectivism: examining one focal chapter across four situated epistemic vantage points, aggregated into a unified thematic subject.

    #>four_readings
    #:reflection #!metacognition
    @measured: ~"./calibration.spw"

    me = student@ch2[sure]{recall}<quiz>
    peer = peer@ch2[unsure]{spacing}<ask>
    later = later@ch2[review]{kept}<exam>
    tutor = tutor@ch2[watch]{gap}<lesson>

    &ch2{recall, spacing, kept, gap}

loops.spw: Collaborative workflow orchestration: concurrent persona execution loops coordinated through serial handoff gates and inter-loop communicative relays.

    #>persona_loops
    #:board #!loops #!production
    @archivist: ~"./archivist.spw"

    reference = ~"./folios/release.spw"
    ahead = #[`the holds`, `the scans`][reg=set]
    loops = {
      archivist@scan{provenance},
      designer@scan{placement},
      editor@scan{caption}
    }
    each = path{~read; *note; ?ask; !hand_back}
    handoff = path{^gather; ?check; !release}
    relay = {archivist.provenance ~> editor.caption}

    ?["What must one loop hand another before it can start?"]{
      ~#expect: `only the caption waits, on provenance`
      !probe{ "list what each loop reads; what another loop writes goes in the handoff" }
    }

gradient.spw: Continuous epistemic gradient: parameterizing decisions along a scalar spectrum between polarized stances, replacing binary dichotomy with nuanced spatial positioning.

    #>gradient_space
    #:board #!gradient

    reference = ~"./plans/index.spw"
    from = archivist@plans{keep}
    to = designer@plans{reshape}
    gradient = #[
      `0.10 keep every line as written`,
      `0.40 keep the dates, rewrite the slices`,
      `0.70 keep the wonders, redraw the order`,
      `0.90 rebuild around the reader`
    ][reg=set]

    ?["Where on this gradient does each plan sit today?"]{
      ~#expect: `most sit near 0.40`
      !probe{ "read each plan's head line and name its place" }
    }

syntax.spw: Syntactic and relational joins: associative company, sequential path order, communicative reach with ~>, perspectival regard, and nested constituent hierarchies.

    #>syntax_stage
    #:showcase #!syntax
    @company: ~"./headings.spw#headings"

    company = {student, classmate, later}
    order = path{~read; *note; ?ask}
    reach = home ~> topics
    regard = student@indexing
    nest = shelf{chip{ring, pill}, card{lifted}}
    line = home[hook]{software.art}(atlas)<record>

headings.spw: Information organization and subject indexing: multiple competing indexing terms held in associative company, preserving ambiguity prior to catalog authorization.

    #>subject_headings
    #:showcase #!indexing #!library

    speaker = I
    wondered = indexing
    headings = {student, classmate, later}@indexing

    ?["Which heading would a catalog keep, and which stay in company?"]{
      ~#expect: `the three stay; the catalog's one term is a later choice`
      !probe{ "read the three names in the brace and say which one a shelf would authorize" }
    }

perform.spw: Dynamic architectural configuration: when a structural pattern performs against an operational slot, the runtime materializes its declared theme consequence.

    #>pattern_performance
    #:showcase #!pattern #!theme
    @line: ~"./syntax.spw#line"

    pattern = pivot
    performs = one.slot
    theme = glass
    line = home[hook]{software.art}<atlas>

    ?["When the pivot performs, which theme should the page take?"]{
      ~#expect: `glass, while one slot moves and the rest stays`
      !probe{ "change theme to matte and watch the field lose its shadow" }
    }

outline.spw: A course four levels deep: terms hold units, units hold weeks, weeks hold what is read and done.

    #>course_outline
    #:outline #!curriculum
    @session: ~"./session.spw"

    course = term{
      unit{
        week{read{chapter, margin}, do{drill, recall}},
        week{read{essay}, do{studio}}
      },
      unit{
        week{read{review}, do{retry}}
      }
    }

rain.spw: One word in four slots: rain as the subject, a part, a scene, and where a line goes.

    #>rain_ledger
    #:study #!identity
    @headings: ~"./headings.spw"

    morning = rain[light]{gutter, path}
    field = soil[wet]{rain, roots}
    song = chorus{verse, bridge}(rain)
    barrel = !water{roof ~> barrel}<rain>

kitchen.spw: Four neighbors under four laws: what lifts, what drifts, what stays, and what will not close.

    #>kitchen_laws
    #:showcase #!physics
    @perform: ~"./perform.spw"

    kitchen = {
      ^bread{flour, water},
      ~soup{beans, salt},
      =spice{cumin, clove},
      ?stock{bones, time}
    }

pantry.spw: A census of one shelf: sixteen things in company, read as a list and as a set of places.

    #>pantry_census
    #:record #!inventory

    pantry = shelf[full]{
      oats, rice, lentils, barley,
      salt, sugar, yeast, honey,
      vinegar, oil, cumin, clove,
      bay, thyme, sage, dill
    }

pipeline.spw: The common data-processing pass, in order: ground the units, fix the schema, keep valid rows, compute, join, group, sum, rank, index, show, and page on. Each step wears the mark that names its job.

    #>order_pipeline
    #:pipeline #!data
    @records: ~"./records.spw#schema"
    @review: ~"./review.spw"

    source = $orders[csv]{id, customer, qty, price}
    steps = path{
      .ground{utc, usd};
      =schema{qty, price};
      ?keep[valid]{qty, price};
      !map{total};
      &join{customers};
      ^group[by]{customer};
      %sum{total};
      *rank[desc]{total};
      #index{customer};
      @show[top]{ten};
      ~next{page}
    }
    run = {source ~> steps ~> report}

    ?["Which step must run before the sum?"]{
      ~#expect: `the keep, so a bad row never reaches %sum`
      !probe{ "move ?keep below %sum and read what the total now counts" }
    }

review.spw: One review point said three ways: by valence, from warm to blocking; by stance, from a question to a requirement, with a confidence; and by register, for a junior, a mid-level or a senior engineer.

    #>review_voice
    #:nuance #!review
    @pipeline: ~"./pipeline.spw#steps"

    point = keep{before ~> sum}

    ^"valence"{
      boon = `Good catch: no bad row reaches the sum.`
      bone = `The keep runs before the sum.`
      bane = `A bad row can still reach the sum.`
      bonk = `The total doubled after this merge.`
      honk = `This blocks the release.`
    }[reg=facet]

    ^"stance"{
      ask = ?point<curious>
      offer = ~point<suggestion>
      need = !point<blocking>
      credit = *point<kept>
      confidence = 0.8
    }[reg=facet]

    ^"register"{
      junior = explain[step]{why, how, try}
      mid = weigh[trade]{cost, option}
      senior = flag[risk]{scope, owner}
    }[reg=facet]

records.spw: The records a software team passes around, each in a line: a schema, a config, an API contract, a dependency graph, a test run, a metric, a diff, a ticket, a trace, and a dated log.

    #>engineering_records
    #:record #!engineering
    @pipeline: ~"./pipeline.spw"

    schema = order{id, customer, qty, price}
    config = checkout[prod]{timeout, retries}
    contract = post[orders]{order ~> receipt}<api>
    deps = service{web ~> api, api ~> db}
    tests = suite[checkout]{pass, fail, skip}
    metric = latency[p95]{checkout}<week>
    diff = change[timeout]{ten ~> thirty}
    ticket = bug[open]{checkout, timeout}<t812>
    trace = request{web ~> api ~> db}<span>

    ^"log"{
     >>[2026-11-14 09:12] error — checkout timed out at 10s
     >>[2026-11-14 09:40] change — timeout raised to 30s
     >>[2026-11-14 10:05] measure — p95 back under 400ms
    }

surfaces.spw: The interactive surfaces of print and of the screen as two censuses, the hand each one asks for, and the print surface each screen surface grew from.

    #>publishing_surfaces
    #:census #!publishing
    @records: ~"./records.spw"

    print = book{
      cover, spine, endpaper, contents,
      spread, margin, footnote, caption,
      pull_quote, index, fold_out, insert
    }
    screen = page{
      link, button, menu, search,
      form, field, dialog, tab,
      scroll, carousel, comment, share,
      player, map, toast, tooltip
    }
    hands = {
      turn{spread, fold_out, insert},
      scan{contents, index, caption},
      tap{link, button, tab, share},
      type{search, field, comment},
      drag{scroll, carousel, map}
    }
    lineage = {
      contents ~> menu, index ~> search,
      footnote ~> tooltip, spread ~> scroll,
      margin ~> comment, insert ~> dialog
    }

primitives.spw: The values and structures most code is built from, each with what it does quickly and what it costs: scalars, then lists, maps and sets, stacks and queues, heaps, trees and graphs.

    #>primitives
    #:census #!computing
    @algorithms: ~"./algorithms.spw"

    scalars = {number, text, flag, none, time}
    array = list[indexed]{read, append}<constant>
    map = table[hashed]{put, get, has}<constant>
    set = table[unique]{add, has}<constant>
    stack = list[last_in]{push, pop}<constant>
    queue = list[first_in]{enqueue, dequeue}<constant>
    heap = tree[ordered]{push, pop_min}<log_n>
    tree = node{value, children}<log_n>
    graph = node{value, edges}<v_plus_e>

    ?["Which structure would you reach for to dedupe a stream?"]{
      ~#expect: `a set, since has is constant`
      !probe{ "count lookups per row with a list, then with a set" }
    }

algorithms.spw: Common algorithms as paths of marked steps: search, sort, walk a graph, slide a window, and remember a subproblem. The cost each one pays rides in the scene.

    #>algorithms
    #:study #!computing
    @primitives: ~"./primitives.spw"
    @pipeline: ~"./pipeline.spw#steps"

    binary_search = path{
      =range{low, high};
      ~halve{mid};
      ?compare{target};
      @return{index}
    }<log_n>
    merge_sort = path{~split{half}; *sort{each}; ^merge{runs}}<n_log_n>
    bfs = path{=queue{start}; ~visit{edges}; #seen{node}}<v_plus_e>
    dfs = path{=stack{start}; ~descend{edges}; #seen{node}}<v_plus_e>
    window = path{=edges{left, right}; ~slide; %sum{inside}}<n>
    memo = path{?seen{subproblem}; !solve; #keep{answer}}<states>

    ?["Which of these answers which page links to which?"]{
      ~#expect: `bfs, one hop at a time from the page you start on`
      !probe{ "walk the site's links from Home and count hops to each page" }
    }

role.spw: One member's skills applied to a role: what they bring, the snippets they kept and where each came from, and what they will build first. A team can read every card and build from the snippets the cards point to.

    #>role_card
    #:role #!team
    @pipeline: ~"./pipeline.spw"
    @records: ~"./records.spw"
    @surfaces: ~"./surfaces.spw"

    role = frontend[mid]{pages, forms, speed}<team>
    brings = skill{a11y, testing, design_handoff}
    kept = #[
      ~"./surfaces.spw#lineage",
      ~"./records.spw#metric",
      ~"./pipeline.spw#steps"
    ][reg=set]
    first = !build[form]{checkout ~> receipt}
    measure = %latency[p95]{before ~> after}

    ?["Which kept snippet does the first build lean on?"]{
      ~#expect: `the lineage, since a form grew from a printed one`
      !probe{ "build the form, then say which snippet you reread twice" }
    }

onboarding.spw: Three paths through the team's other four files: what a junior, a mid-level and a senior engineer read first, change, and teach in their first week.

    #>team_onboarding
    #:plan #!onboarding
    @pipeline: ~"./pipeline.spw"
    @review: ~"./review.spw#register"
    @records: ~"./records.spw"
    @surfaces: ~"./surfaces.spw"

    junior = path{~read{pipeline}; !change{one_step}; ?ask{review}}
    mid = path{^own{pipeline}; ~read{records}; !review{peer}}
    senior = path{*shape{surfaces}; =set{contract}; !teach{review}}
    week = {junior, mid, senior} ~> demo

    ?["What can each of them change by Friday?"]{
      ~#expect: `a junior one step, a mid one record, a senior one contract`
      !probe{ "each says in one line what they changed and where it shows" }
    }
